bib.title: The Unreasonable Effectiveness of Deep Features as a Perceptual Metric

question: How well do deep network features (supervised, self-supervised, unsupervised, random) agree with human perceptual similarity judgments compared with classic metrics such as L2, SSIM and FSIM?
hypothesis: Perceptual similarity is an emergent property shared across deep visual representations, not a special function of its own.
contributions: A large-scale, highly varied perceptual similarity dataset with 484k human judgments, including real algorithm outputs and JND tests
Deep features from supervised, self-supervised and unsupervised objectives model low-level perceptual similarity well, outperforming widely used metrics
Network architecture alone does not account for performance: untrained nets do much worse
Performance can be improved by calibrating feature responses of a pretrained network with the data

method.summary: The authors collect BAPPS, 64x64 patch triplets with 2AFC human judgments and a JND test, and score distances from deep features (unit-normalised per-channel, squared l2, spatial mean, summed over layers) by agreement with humans. They also learn per-channel weights (lin), fine-tune (tune) or train from scratch (scratch) with a small judgment-prediction net, giving LPIPS.
method.task: perceptual image patch similarity (2AFC agreement with humans)

datasets.name: BAPPS 2AFC-Distort train
datasets.preprocessing: 64x64 patches, two distortions applied per reference (traditional: 20 distortions + 308 composed; CNN-based: 96 denoising autoencoders trained 1 epoch on 1.3M ImageNet)

datasets.name: BAPPS 2AFC-Real Alg val
datasets.split: superres 10.9k, frame interp, video deblur, colorization; 5 judgments each
datasets.source: NTIRE 2017/Div2K, Davis Middlebury, video deblurring dataset, ImageNet
datasets.preprocessing: random scales for frame interp and colorization

datasets.name: BAPPS JND-Distort val
datasets.preprocessing: patches shown 1 s each with 250 ms gap

models.name: Self-supervised/unsupervised AlexNet variants (BiGAN, Puzzle, Split-Brain, Watching, k-means) and random Gaussian net
LPIPS (lin/tune/scratch) over Squeeze/Alex/VGG
models.architecture: backbone plus channel weights w and a small net G (two 32-channel FC-ReLU, 1-channel FC, sigmoid)
models.init_from: lin: pretrained frozen; tune: pretrained, all weights trained; scratch: random Gaussian

training.objective: binary cross-entropy of G(d(x,x0),d(x,x1)) against human preference h (Eq 2); ranking loss tried in preliminary experiments and was worse
training.lr: 1e-4 for 5 epochs, then linear decay over 5 epochs
training.lr_schedule: 5 epochs at initial lr, 5 epochs linear decay
training.regularisation: channel weights w constrained non-negative by projection every iteration; split judgments give soft target 0.5

other.inferred: inferred: training uses 64x64 patch triplets from the 2AFC-Distort train set

inference.samples: 5 human judgments per val triplet; 2 per train triplet; single run reported, no seeds

parameters.distance: d(x,x0)=sum_l 1/(HlWl) sum_hw ||wl*(yhat_l - yhat0_l)||_2^2 on channel-unit-normalised features

metrics.name: 2AFC score
metrics.definition: agreement with all human judgments per triplet (e.g. 4 of 5 votes for x0 gives 80% credit); human score p^2+(1-p)^2

metrics.name: JND mAP
metrics.definition: patch pairs ordered by metric, precision-recall AUC for same/different

metrics.name: Spearman correlation on TID2013
metrics.definition: rank correlation with MOS at resolutions 128-512

eval.protocol: Mechanical Turk, sentinels (approx. 90% of Turkers passed at least 14 of 15). Per-subset and All scores in Table 5. No significance tests or seeds reported.

evidence.quote: We train with 5 epochs at initial learning rate 10−4, 5 epochs with linear decay, and batch size 50.

results.claim: Humans are 73.9% consistent on the 2AFC task averaged over all 6 test sets (the ceiling).
results.setup: BAPPS validation sets (traditional, CNN-based, 4 real-algorithm sets), 5 judgments per triplet; human score = expected agreement p^2+(1-p)^2
results.quote: Averaged across all 6 test sets, humans are 73.9% consistent.

results.claim: Out-of-the-box supervised nets (SqueezeNet, AlexNet, VGG) score 68.6, 68.9 and 67.0 on 2AFC across all six sets.
results.setup: ImageNet-supervised nets, mean of 5 conv layers' unit-normalised features, cosine distance (w=1), no calibration; all 6 test sets
results.quote: the supervised networks perform at about the same level to each other, at 68.6%, 68.9%, and 67.0%
results.note: Text order is Squeeze, Alex, VGG.

results.claim: L2, SSIM and FSIMc score 63.2, 63.1 and 63.8 on 2AFC across all six sets.
results.table: Table 5, rows L2, SSIM, FSIMc, column All

results.claim: Learned (LPIPS) variants reach 69.2-70.2 on all six sets, only about 1-2 points above uncalibrated supervised nets and still below the human 73.9.
results.setup: Best LPIPS row, Alex-scratch; trained on traditional+CNN distortions of BAPPS, evaluated on all 6 sets
results.table: Table 5, row Alex – scratch, column All (second All)
results.note: Squeeze-lin 70.0, VGG-scratch 70.0, Alex-lin 69.8, VGG-tune 69.8, VGG-lin 69.2. These LPIPS rows have an advantage on the in-distribution distortion columns.

results.claim: On real algorithm outputs, off-the-shelf nets start at 64.0, 65.0 and 62.6; linear calibration improved 11 of 12 scores (+1.1, +0.3, +1.5).
results.setup: Squeeze/Alex/VGG on superres, frame interp, deblur, colorization
results.quote: The SqueezeNet, AlexNet, and VGG architectures start at 64.0%, 65.0%, and 62.6%, respectively.

results.claim: Fine-tuning all weights from a pretrained net improves distortion-set accuracy (VGG-tune 81.4, near human 82.6) but lowers transfer to real algorithms.
results.setup: VGG-tune on BAPPS traditional+CNN val sets
results.quote: (80.6% and 81.4% for Alex – tune and VGG – tune, respectively), is almost equal to human performance of 82.6%

results.claim: 2AFC and JND scores correlate at rho 0.928 across methods.
results.setup: AlexNet-like architectures, averaged over traditional and CNN-based distortions; JND scored as mAP

results.claim: 2AFC perceptual score correlates .640 with PASCAL classification and .363 with detection across methods.
results.setup: AlexNet-like architectures; PASCAL results from Zhang et al. 2017

results.claim: Random Gaussian-weight network gets 64.3 overall, only 1.2 above L2-ish baselines; unsupervised k-means gets 66.6.
results.table: Table 5, row Net (Random) Gaussian, column All
results.note: Text says random nets 'do not yield much improvement'.

results.claim: On traditional distortions FSIMc gets 61.4 and L2 59.9 while classification nets get 73.3, 70.6, 70.1.
results.setup: BAPPS traditional distortions, Squeeze/Alex/VGG out of box

results.claim: Linear calibration learns only 1472 parameters for VGG; for Alex-lin about half of the 1152 weights are zero.

limits: Judgments are on 64x64 patches, low-level similarity only; high-level semantic similarity not covered.
2AFC is cognitively penetrable; JND used as a check.
Humans collected in the wild on AMT, only 2 judgments per train triplet.
LPIPS gains over uncalibrated nets are small on real algorithms (+0.3 to +1.5) and fine-tuning hurts transfer.
SSIM not designed for geometric distortions, which the dataset includes, which may inflate the deep-vs-classic gap.
Directly fitting a function to human judgments failed to generalize (negative result).

terms.definition: two alternative forced choice: which of two distortions is closer to a reference
just noticeable difference: whether a reference and a distorted patch look the same or different
Learned Perceptual Image Patch Similarity: deep-feature distance with learned channel weights

lineage.work: Perceptual losses (Johnson et al.; Gatys style transfer)
lineage.note: asks how perceptual VGG-feature losses are
